writingStyle.description: Language quality guidance injected into all LLM prompts
writingStyle.titles: 3-6 words. Plain noun phrase that names the specific error. No parentheticals or clarifications inside parentheses. Write the error directly: 'Did Not Flip the Second Fraction' — never 'Did Not Flip the Second Fraction (no reciprocal)'.
writingStyle.descriptions: 2-3 sentences maximum. Keep it concrete and specific. Do NOT start every sentence with 'Students' — vary the subject. Good openers: the error itself ('Slope and intercept get swapped...'), a conditional ('When reading y = mx + b, the two numbers...'), or the consequence ('The result is...'). One idea per sentence. No hedging words (often, typically, usually, tend to). Do not restate the same idea in different words. Write for a classroom teacher, not a researcher.
writingStyle.instructionalMoves: Write in short, scannable chunks. Use plain conversational language — imagine a teacher reading this quickly between classes. Break steps into separate sentences. Avoid dense paragraphs. No academic or clinical language. Active voice. Each instruction should be one action: 'Show students two worked examples side by side.' not 'Teachers should consider presenting students with two worked examples simultaneously for comparison purposes.'
writingStyle.successIndicators: Start each with an action verb. Describe observable student behavior only. 10 words max per indicator.

analysis.description: Rationale dimensions carried over from the former microcoachv2LLMAnalysis. Used by microcoachv2LLMGenInstrNeed to explain and rank each need, not to select or filter misconceptions.

misconceptionScoring.description: Weights for the composite that orders priorityRank across misconceptions. Weights should sum to 1.0.

conceptualSeverityScale.description: Guide for the LLM when estimating conceptual severity: 1.0 = structural conceptual misunderstanding of the math concept; 0.6 = mixed conceptual and procedural; 0.3 = procedural/execution error only

confidenceScoring.description: Confidence modifies existing scoring dimensions rather than adding a new one.
confidenceScoring.prevalenceAdjustment: discount correct rate when avgConfidenceCorrect < lowAvgConfidenceCorrectThreshold

genInstrNeed.description: microcoachv2LLMGenInstrNeed — for each misconception from microcoachv2LLMGenMisconception, states the instructional need (what students most need to understand, examine, or do next mathematically) and the rationale built from the classroom evidence. Internal reasoning step that will drive template selection; not teacher-facing.
needKinds: locating and understanding the first point where valid reasoning breaks down
understanding why an incorrect response is tempting or reasonable and revising the underlying reasoning
comparing meaningfully different approaches to make mathematical thinking visible
diagnosing an underlying mathematical issue, developing a repair, and checking whether the repair works
investigating, defending, challenging, or refining a mathematical claim
individually or in small teams engaging with targeted mathematical questions that elicit and surface student thinking for subsequent discussion and reasoning

worked.misconception: Multiplying powers with the same base requires multiplying the exponents
worked.instructionalNeed: Test the apparent rule, examine why it initially seems to work, and use the meaning of exponents to construct the correct generalization.
